help.tips[0].examples[0].en: At first I only wanted to shop, then I suddenly met my boss in the supermarket.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: In the end I went home with a full bag and a day off on Monday.
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: haben stays in the Präteritum when you tell a past story: ich hatte. Letzten Samstag rules out the present.
help.tips[0].en.text: Zuerst … Dann … Plötzlich … Am Ende … — one past verb per step. war, hatte and wollte in the Präteritum; the other verbs in the Perfekt (spoken) or the Präteritum (written style) — both are correct, and mixing them this way is normal.
help.tips[0].en.title: Tell it in order
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: The bread is cut, then it's spread with butter.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: First the water is boiled, then the tea is put in.
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: A process step is an action, so it takes the werden-passive, and Kartoffeln is plural: werden geschält.
help.tips[1].en.text: Wie wird Kaffee gemacht? – Zuerst wird das Wasser gekocht. Dann wird der Kaffee gemahlen. Danach wird … The participle closes every sentence.
help.tips[1].en.title: Describe a process in the passive
help.hookEn: Tell what happened last weekend and explain how something is made, out loud, in three minutes.
help.introEn: A three-minute checkpoint on the first half of this module, in your own AI assistant with voice on: telling something that happened, and describing how something is done. The tutor asks Was ist letztes Wochenende passiert? and Wie wird … gemacht?, and listens for the past forms — war, hatte, ging, kam, wurde — and for the passive frame (wird … gemacht, wurde … gebaut). Speak in whole sentences with the signposts (zuerst, dann, plötzlich, am Ende) and let the verbs land at the end of the passive sentences; the score and corrections come at the end (say 'Ende' if you need to finish early).
help.rememberEn[0]: Story: signposts + past verbs. Process: wird + participle.
help.rememberEn[1]: Say the participle at the end; don't stop before it.
